comparedAgainst: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Overview (MDN, fetched: diagrams and a request/response sample, no runnable code, no measurement)
A second page (https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/dns/) returned 404 and was not used as evidence; the comparison rests on one successful fetch plus the site's own WRITER_GUIDE phone rules
justification: Presentation is close to MDN quality and the concept is better illustrated than in MDN's overview: three figures that each carry information (Figure 1 sequence bands with RTT labels, Figure 2 chunked-body byte accounting, Figure 3 layer wrapping with byte counts), all correct in dark theme with the accent color still separating encrypted arrows, all drawn at 360 units so nothing is faded or cut at 390 px. Reading rhythm is good for 5,750 words and 32 minutes: prose, one program, an output panel, then interpretation, with only three callouts (In .NET, Common pitfall, Info) that each carry content, five collapsed exercises of different forms placed mid-flow, a compact timing table that fits at 390 px, and a 27-item dated Sources list. Heading hierarchy is clean (one H1, specific H2s, H3s only under the long TCP and TLS sections), no boilerplate headings, output panels are 40 columns or less. The round-1 major on the three-column layer-model table is fixed (now a four-item list). Held below 8.5 because the round-1 major on phone clipping is only partly fixed: in the SNI experiment the host-name argument that the prose calls 'the only thing that differed' is under the fade at 390 px. Smaller nits: British spellings on an American-spelling site (one of them inside Figure 1), a three-line H2 on phones, and the phone hero pushing the first paragraph to the bottom of the first screen (shell). Real numbers from report.json and lighthouse.json: Lighthouse 95/100/100/100, zero console errors, zero broken links, mobileOverflowPx 0; the only failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder. Performance 95 comes from FCP/LCP/Speed Index of 2.4 s on the simulated mobile profile with TBT 0 and CLS 0; the audit also flagged 'document latency, est. savings of 170 KiB', likely compression on the local preview server, so performance may be understated or vary; the orchestrator should still re-measure serially.
